steps.content:
One Week Later
Auction

steps.speaker: Receptionist
steps.content: Miss Ellington, thank you for joining us this evening. Our records show you've registered with one companion. Would that be this person beside you?

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Yes, this is my assistant.

steps.speaker: Receptionist
steps.content: Perfect. We'll ensure everything is ready for you both. There's still some time before the auction begins, but in the meantime, you're welcome to explore the exhibition hall, where a selection of tonight's pieces is on display.

steps.speaker: Receptionist
steps.content: When the event is about to start, a member of our team will personally escort you to your seats.
Thalia offers a polite, professional smile before turning on her heel and striding toward the exhibition hall, her pace brisk and purposeful.

With a flick of her fingers, she signals for you to keep up, navigating through the space with practiced ease. She heads straight for the exhibits at the back, her attention already fixed on their details.
You trail behind, your gaze skimming over the displays. None of them match what you're searching for, so your focus drifts instead to the venue itself.
Despite the crowd, the cavernous space swallows sound whole, leaving only the sharp, solitary click of heels against polished floors.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I've attended quite a few elite gatherings in Eastside myself, but I've never been to this place before.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: The booking process here is incredibly complicated—applications, reviews, and a waiting list of at least six months. Honestly, most people wouldn't bother with all that trouble.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: A six-month wait... Does Eastside really have that many events going on year-round?

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Oh, it's just to make the place seem more exclusive. You know, "A place even money can't book"—sounds impressive, right? In my line of work, we call this "hunger marketing."

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: But in reality? If the owner considers you valuable enough, you can just give him a call, and he'll personally come pick you up the very next day.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Sounds like you're speaking from experience?

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Well, this place isn't far from my home. Every year, my father would...
At the mention of her father, Thalia flinches, a sharp, involuntary reaction like biting down on a needle. The words die in her throat. You can't help but look.
She catches your gaze. For a heartbeat, her lips tremble, betraying some unspoken tension, before she sculpts them into that familiar, practiced smile.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Were you and your father not on good terms?

You come to a halt before an Outland oil painting. In the depicted scene, a man clad in a sumptuous robe sits at a table, his plate holding nothing but a single stale crust of black bread. His eyes dart over his shoulder, shadowed with unease, as though he fears unseen watchers.
Beneath the frame, the title reads: "A Nobleman's Meal."
Thalia's fingers brush the edge of the information plaque, her laugh low and humorless.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: He... There's really not much worth saying about him.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: My father was the typical spoiled rich kid, never accomplished a thing. As far back as I can remember, his only job was... indulging himself.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: To him, money just appeared out of thin air. He lent huge sums to so-called relatives and friends, and when he finally asked for it back? They just laughed in his face.
Thalia lets out another cold snort.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: I remember begging one of my friends for help... but she told me her parents had warned her to stay away from our entire family.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: That was how I found out he'd already gone to them for money. She said I was just like him back then.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: I was just like him... just like him...
Her voice drips with bitterness and pain.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: But... I'm nothing like that man. Just look—

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Look who's standing here now.
As Thalia speaks, she lifts her chin, her smile bold and unrestrained.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: I've worked so hard for so long... all for this moment.
You suddenly remember her words back in the interrogation room.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...That's why you have to attend the auction?

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: What? You think that's not a "noble enough" reason?
Catching your expression, Thalia's smile slowly fades.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Save the pity. If we're talking holier-than-thou, I used to be way worse than you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No, I just find it hard to believe.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: To just attend this auction, you accepted the Bureau's surveillance, letting me put the shackles on you. You'd rather give up all your personal freedom just to stand here again.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But does a single auction really define someone's status and worth?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And let's be honest, I'm not exactly "elite" either, yet here I am, right beside you. That kind of judgment seems way too arbitrary.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: ...Are you done talking?

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: You have no idea...
Thalia lowers her voice, forcing out each word through gritted teeth.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: I was homeless at eighteen, sleeping on the streets, taking humiliation from anyone who felt like kicking me when I was down... So yeah, excuse me if I don't feel bad crawling my way back here. You don't get it. You've never had everything ripped away.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I have no idea, that's true. But Thalia, by standing here, do you really think you've earned back the respect you want?

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: You're my assistant now. Remember to call me Miss Ellington.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Does being addressed that way make you feel any better?
Thalia doesn't respond, only glaring at you. Perhaps it's that so-called noble dignity of hers, restraining her from losing her temper in public. After all, such an outburst would be beneath her.
Oh, Miss Ellington!
An unfamiliar voice breaks the silence between you. You turn toward the sound to see a young man striding toward you, his burgundy satin suit whispering of money.
He extends his hand toward Thalia, his diamond cufflinks glinting like ice under the light.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: She wanted happiness, and I wanted her to have it without having to feel guilty about leaving me behind. So I erased our shared memories of us arguing, of us hating and hurting each other.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Pardon me, you are...?

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: Haha, you probably don't know me. Just call me Charlie. I'm with Madison Electronics Group.
He pulls a business card from his wallet and hands it to Thalia.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: I've always been a huge fan. Bumping into you here feels like such a lucky break. I couldn't resist coming over to say hello.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Oh, I see! Thank you so much for your support.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: Honestly, it's because your content is exceptional. I rarely have time for streams, but yours? I make an exception. Your recommendations are so refined. It's a breath of fresh air compared to those streamers from the smaller districts.
Thalia's eyebrow twitches imperceptibly, yet her practiced smile never wavers, her silence speaking volumes.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: Look, let's not even go there... Anyway, I'd be honored to have the chance to connect.
Thalia reads between the lines and retrieves a business card from her purse, offering it in return.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Oh, please, no need to be so formal. If anything, the honor is all mine.
Seizing the moment, the nearby guests—who had been watching intently—swarm in, eager to join the conversation and "connect" with her.

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: ...Well then, it's settled, Miss Ellington. I hope fame won't make you forget the little people, haha...

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Of course not. Look, I've kept your card safe and sound, haven't I?

steps.speaker: Guest C
steps.content: Miss Ellington, would you mind sharing where you got that outfit of yours too?
Thalia basks in her triumph, radiant and self-assured, while you linger silently at her side, the very picture of a devoted assistant.

Yet from the shadows of a nearby corner, you catch a group of strangers staring this way, their hushed whispers threading through the clamor of the crowd. Their muted, somber attire stands in stark contrast to the glittering opulence around Thalia.
Test, test... Ladies and gentlemen...

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: Greetings, everyone. I'll be your host for today's auction. We're about to begin, so please follow the instructions from our staff and take your seats promptly.

The moment the announcement echoes through the hall, the crowd around you disperses in every direction. You fall into step behind the staff, trailing them into a smaller, dimly lit chamber tucked away from the main hall.

The auction begins without fanfare, its opening acts a parade of mediocrity. Beside you, Thalia's fingers drum an impatient rhythm against her armrest—contempt in every tap—while your own idle tapping mirrors only boredom.
As the auction reaches its midpoint, you finally spot what you came here for.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Just as I thought, many of these pieces are on the contraband catalog, like that pair of porcelain plates.
Hearing your words, Thalia pulls a pen from her handbag and quietly clicks down the clip. Then, she raises a finger to her lips, gesturing for you to stay quiet.
Only when the porcelain collection finds its new owner does she finally break her silence, waving the pen.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: It might come in handy for your investigation later.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You carry a recording pen with you?

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: When I meet with clients privately, I like to record our conversations.
With Thalia providing cover, you send notifications to the Bureau and FAC, requesting them to dispatch personnel to the venue immediately to investigate both the buyers and sellers here.
Seeing your message go through, Thalia visibly eases. She crosses her legs, sinks into her seat with effortless grace, and flips through the auction catalog, a faint smile playing on her lips.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's not over yet.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: But I'm already in the clear.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Oh, and if your people show up before the auction ends, don't drag me into it, okay? I don't want to miss the final item.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: There's something good at the end?
Thalia lets out a soft snort.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: The final item is always the real highlight, and it never appears in the catalog. I guess you could call it a little surprise.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Did you pick up your sales skills from places like this?
Thalia glances up at you with a smile but remains silent.
The auction races toward its conclusion. At last, she sets aside the catalog and straightens in her seat, her attention fixed on the stage.

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: And now, it's time for the final highlight of today's event.
A staff member wheels in a small cart, its contents hidden beneath a sleek black silk drape.
Even before the reveal, the audience erupts into applause—proof enough, as Thalia said, that being chosen as the grand finale speaks volumes about this item's value.
With a flourish, the host signals the staff member.

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: Please.

The black cloth slips away, unveiling an emerald hummingbird brooch perched atop a velvet stand. Bathed in the spotlight, the creature's jeweled eyes glint with an almost lifelike intensity, its wings catching the light in a dazzling dance of refracted color—as if, at any moment, it might take flight.
The brilliance of it floods your senses, its radiance undeniable. No wonder this piece is the auction's crown jewel.

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: This is the last auction item for today: the Emerald Hummingbird Brooch.
You turn to Thalia, a question on your lips, only to freeze. She sits rigid, her usual poise shattered, every trace of warmth drained from her face.
Her gaze is locked onto the brooch, unblinking, her fingers clenched around the armrests with such force that her knuckles stand out like bone against skin.
And immediately, your question is answered.

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: This exquisite brooch was personally commissioned by the founding patriarch of the Ellington family, crafted by the world's finest master jeweler, for their eyes alone.

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: It became their crest, a symbol of diligence, prosperity, and legacy... which is why, for generations, it has never left family hands.

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: ...Though, given the Ellington name... one might call that symbolism... ironic.
At this point, the host lets out a few dry chuckles, and the audience responds with scattered, half-hearted laughter.

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: Nevertheless, artistry knows no scandal. This remains a masterpiece, untouched by time. A chance like this is truly unrepeatable. Now, let the bidding begin!
The moment he finishes speaking, the crowd erupts into a frenzy. People around you lean forward, scrambling to place their bids.
Then the air shivers. A faint ripple of energy. Your instincts scream at you, and you lunge for Thalia's wrist. But you're too late. Her bidding paddle is already raised.

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: We have five million from Number 28!
The number she calls out is so absurd that the entire venue falls dead silent.

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: Five million, going once...
Thalia shakes off your grip, her sleeve slipping from your fingers.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: My father sold this brooch long ago to settle his debts... but I never found out who bought it...
Her voice trembles, but more unsettling are the waves of Mania rolling off her, growing stronger, wilder.

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: Five million, going twice...

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: All this time, I've been searching... I've reclaimed everything else, but this... this was the one thing I couldn't find. And the most important one...

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: Five million, going three times...

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: I won't leave it behind. It belongs with me. No one else has the right to keep it. Go ahead, laugh if you want...
Almost simultaneously...

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: And... sold!

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Laugh all you want!
The moment the gavel falls, the Mania fluctuations cease abruptly. Thalia releases a long, shaky breath and sags against the back of her chair, as if the tension has drained from her all at once.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Are you alright?

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: I'm fine. Sorry, that was unbecoming of me.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Thank you. Earlier I...
She seems about to say something more, but two figures approach you both.

steps.speaker: Staff Member
steps.content: Miss Thalia? This gentleman represents the seller of the item you've just won. They'd like a word with you, if you're available.
You and Thalia stand up together, and she nods politely to him.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Good day.
To your surprise, the man doesn't respond. He just stares, his silence heavy between you. Thalia clears her throat and finally speaks up, her voice tinged with awkwardness.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: May I ask when the formal transaction process will begin?

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Our sincerest apologies, but Madam has had a change of heart and will no longer be offering the brooch for sale.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: What? Are you kidding me?

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: We sincerely apologize for this situation. In accordance with the auction house's policies, we'll honor the breach of contract terms and provide the agreed compensation.
Despite his words, the man doesn't even bother to nod.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: I'm truly sorry as well, but I just can't accept this solution. Compensation isn't what I'm after; I want that brooch, and nothing else.
Their hostility is unmistakable. You grab Thalia's wrist, pressing down firmly to steady her. She inhales sharply, fingers curling into fists before exhaling through clenched teeth.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: ...The price isn't a concern, but I won't accept leaving with nothing. Please let the madam know that I'd like to speak with her directly.
Then you catch it: the faintest twitch at the corner of the man's mouth. A ghost of a smile, there and gone.

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Then let me check with Madam first, if you don't mind.
He turns away, hand pressed to his earpiece as he murmurs something too low to hear. Within seconds, he's facing you again.
—You think that was a bit too fast.

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Madam has agreed to see you. Right this way, please.
You immediately step forward to follow, but the man's arm blocks your path.

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Miss Ellington alone will suffice.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...We haven't actually introduced ourselves, have we?
Thalia catches on to the issue as well, and you quickly exchange a glance.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: I need my assistant with me.

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: In that case, there's nothing to discuss.
Thalia turns to you, her gaze searching for your input. At that same moment, your phone vibrates in your pocket. The operatives have likely arrived.
Unease tightens in your chest, but you know nothing will deter her. Not when the brooch is within reach. With a reluctant nod, you watch as she follows the assistant away.
[Empty Shot]

The VIP room is bathed in low light, its shadows deepened by the faint glow of a few lamps at the door. The guests, clad in dark formalwear, melt seamlessly into the dimness, the occasional flicker of their cigarettes cutting through the gloom like distant fireflies.
Thalia stands beneath the light, hesitating over whether to speak first, when a voice from the past reaches her, one she hasn't heard in years.
Well, well... look who it is. Thalia. Darling, has it really been that long?

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: ...Kara?
Something stirs in the shadows, then the woman called Kara steps forward, her face betraying no surprise as she meets Thalia's gaze.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: What's with the cold shoulder? Don't tell me you've forgotten me already.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: ...It's been a long time.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: How long has it been since we stood together like this? It really brings back memories.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Look at you...
As the woman speaks, she inches closer, her hand reaching toward Thalia.
In a flash, Thalia seizes her wrist and locks eyes with her, gaze icy.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Don't you think it's a little late to be saying that now?

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Oh, darling, you're not still holding a grudge, are you?

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: How could I ever forget? Kara, we were close friends for over ten years. And in all that time, I only asked you for help once...
[Empty Shot]

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Kara...? You came for me? I knew it... I knew you would help me!

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Ugh, Thalia, let go of me. And what is that smell?

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: What? I don't... I don't smell anything...

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: The smell of Syndicans...

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Kara, please, just let me come with you! I only need a place to stay for a little while, I swear. Just until I can find a job... I'll work hard and pay you back, every penny! Please...

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Gosh, keep your voice down! You're making a scene, just like your father did when he came begging at our door. It's so embarrassing. My father said we absolutely cannot let your family drag us down like this.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Kara...? What are you saying? I thought you... wanted to help me?

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Help you how? I just wanted to see how far you'd fall. Tell me, Thalia, what will you become down in Syndicate?

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: And spare me the "hard work" speech. You've become just like those Syndicans—all talk, no results... Honestly, being seen with you is mortifying.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Kara, don't say that. I won't... Wait! ...Kara! Kara!
[Empty Shot]
Thalia's lips curl into a bitter smile, her voice sharp as a blade.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Looks like you've become exactly what you were always meant to be.

Kara doesn't answer. Her brow furrows, confusion flickering in her eyes. The words sound sardonic, but their meaning slips through her grasp. Whatever Thalia is referring to, it's long buried in the past, forgotten.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: ...Forget it.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: I didn't come here just to chat about the past. My brooch... you've been holding onto it all this time?
Kara lets out a soft hum.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: You know, after you left, I started missing you a little. Then I remembered this little brooch tucked away in our cabinet. The one your father pawned off to us.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Now that the bid is mine, you can return it to me.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Oh, but I've changed my mind. I suddenly find this brooch quite charming from every angle. I can't possibly part with it now.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Kara! You know exactly how much that means to me...

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Darling, of course I know that. But why would I care?

The VIP room plunges into dead silence. All eyes lock onto the spectacle unfolding before them. They wait—poised on the edge of delight—for the punchline to land, ready to erupt into laughter. And the star of this cruel joke is none other than Thalia Ellington herself.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: ...How much do you want? Just name your price.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: I know you can afford it now. But money? Everyone has that.
She reaches out and lightly pats Thalia's cheek.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Has all that fan adoration gone straight to your head? You think just because you can claw back some money, you can buy back your dignity too?

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Honestly, Thalia, how long do you expect to keep this up? Smiling like some desperate salesgirl, peddling your tacky little trinkets to strangers who'll forget you tomorrow?

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Do you think you're still worthy of wearing that brooch? If your grandfather saw what you've turned into, do you think he'd let you disgrace the Ellington name like this?
Kara's tone shifts suddenly, softening into gentle persuasion.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Thalia... I was too young to help you before. That's why you fell so far.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: But now, I'm offering you a real chance, to reclaim your place, your family's honor...

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: To earn back the right to wear this brooch. And when you do? I'll put it in your hands myself.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: So, what do you say?
Her friend's gaze burns with intensity, every word dripping with raw, heartfelt anguish, yet beneath each sentence lurks something colder, sharper. That familiar flicker of manipulation.
Thalia's thoughts blur. The words cling to her, heavy and disorienting. How much of it was real?
Her fingers dig into her own arm, nails pressing hard into her skin.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: ...What do you want from me?
Kara raises one finger.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: I only need you to do one thing. Something you're best at.
Kara raises her hand with a smile, summoning her assistant to her side.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: I happen to have a rather... delicate collection on my hands. The usual sales channels are... unavailable, so selling them requires a certain finesse.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: But you—our star influencer—could make this vanish with a single livestream. For someone of your caliber, this should be effortless, no?

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: ...Show me your goods first.
The assistant brings a thick catalog to Thalia, flipping through its pages with methodical precision.

A low, creeping unease has been tugging at her since earlier. But now, as she stares at the inventory laid bare before her, that feeling sharpens into something undeniable, solidifying like lead in her chest.
Every item matches. This is the exact same catalog as the Mania-contaminated contraband seized by the FAC, down to the very piece that had once been delivered to her studio.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: This is... Heh, so from the very beginning, this is all just a trap...
Kara dramatically places her hand over her chest, putting on a wounded expression.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Darling, now you're just breaking my heart. I've been racking my brain trying to think of how to help you.
Having said that, she immediately slips back into that perfect smile, raising her hand to signal the assistant to put the catalog away.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Where did you get these?

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: I've been in this business for years. I have my own connections.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Do you even realize how dangerous this is? Is it the money? These things could hurt you, everyone around you—

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Oh my, are you worried about me?

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: ...Don't flatter yourself.
The woman shakes her head with a smile.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: The truth is, I only do this for the thrill of it.
As she speaks, the woman takes on a wistful, melancholic expression.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: You've lived the gilded life, Thalia. Endless studies, tedious social circuits, more money than you could ever spend. Everything is handed to you the moment you snap your fingers...

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Except for one thing. That is... anything to do with Mania.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: My only regret is that I'm not a Sinner.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Alright, back to business. I'll be straight with you: this batch is dirty, and if you're not careful, you'll drown in it. Then again... if you can move it all? Well, that'd prove you're as capable as you claim, wouldn't it?

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Do this, and I'll honor every promise I've made.
The assistant has already prepared the transfer contract, with the donor's name already neatly signed. Only the recipient's line remains blank.
With polished courtesy, he presses the pen into Thalia's hand, his grip firm enough to leave no room for refusal.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Sign. I don't think you have any reason to refuse.
Her palm grows damp, the pen slipping in her grasp. As she raises it, her wrist jerks involuntarily.
The pen clatters to the floor, spinning away before coming to a stop.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Pick it up.
Thalia stares at it, her jaw clenched so tightly her chin trembles. After a weighted pause, she steadies herself, then reaches into her purse with shivering hands and withdraws her own pen.
Just as the tip touches paper, the woman seizes her wrist.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Oh, by the way, don't try anything clever.

steps.speaker: Gang Leader
steps.content: Let's be clear. That brooch of yours? It's contaminated now, too. The moment you report me and they start digging, it'll be confiscated right along with the rest. So if you ever want to see it again... don't try to play games with me. Understood?

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: If I can corner you this easily, imagine what else I could do. Ruin isn't even the half of it.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: But why go there? Just help me move these pieces quietly, and we'll call it even.

steps.speaker: Kara
steps.content: Thalia, I mean it. I do want to help you. And I'd love for us to be close again, just like before.
Thalia looks up, her gaze locking onto her former friend with quiet intensity. Then, without warning, she breaks into a wide, dazzling grin.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: I know. After all, we were best friends.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: Of course I'll sign it.
With deliberate flourish, she lifts her hand and writes down the name she wears like a crown—Thalia Ellington—before folding her arms against her chest.

steps.speaker: Thalia
steps.content: To a successful partnership.
